model.criterion: Plasticity-based preservation failure occurs when maximum PEEQ across shell elements and thickness integration points reaches 0.002, without a minimum damaged volume. Elastic buckling alone does not satisfy this criterion. An additional functional collapse criterion applies when total pad-backing closure reaches d0 - 2h during bilateral contact, where d0 is the initial recorded contact spacing and h is wall thickness. This approximates opposite-wall contact and loss of usable space, not residual indentation after unloading.
model.basis: The published resin model is fitted to a 25 MPa yield stress.

assessment_criteria.criterion: Plasticity-based preservation fails when max PEEQ ≥ 0.002 over the object shell elements and through-thickness integration points. No minimum affected-volume fraction is required; purely elastic buckling does not satisfy this criterion.

Separate functional-collapse criterion: preservation fails if total pad-backing closure Δ_b ≥ d_0 − 2h while bilateral pad contact is maintained. Here d_0 is the initial recorded contact-point separation and h is wall thickness. This approximates opposite-wall contact and loss of usable space, rather than measuring residual indentation after unloading.
